abstract.text:
Abstract—Calculation of static voltage stability margin
(SVSM) of AC/DC power systems with lots of renewable energy
sources (RESs) integration requires consideration of uncertain
load growth and renewable energy generation output. This paper
presents a bi-level optimal power ﬂow (BLOPF) model to identify
the worst-case SVSM of an AC/DC power system with line
commutation converter-based HVDC and multi-terminal voltage
sourced converter-based HVDC transmission lines. Constraints
of uncertain load growth’s hypercone model and control mode
switching of DC converter stations are considered in the BLOPF
model. Moreover, uncertain RES output ﬂuctuations are de-
scribed as intervals, and two three-level optimal power ﬂow
(TLOPF) models are established to identify interval bounds
of the system worst-case SVSM. The two TLOPF models are
both transformed into max–min bi-level optimization models
according to independent characteristics of different uncertain
variables. Then, transforming the inner level model into its dual
form, max–min BLOPF models are simpliﬁed to single-level
optimization models for direct solution. Calculation results on
the modiﬁed IEEE-39 bus AC/DC case and an actual large-scale
AC/DC case in China indicate correctness and efﬁciency of the
proposed identiﬁcation method.

introduction.text:
I. I NTRODUCTION
N
OW ADAYS, LCC-HVDC and multi-terminal voltage
sourced converter-based HVDC (MTVSC-HVDC) trans-
mission technologies are widely used in actual power
grids [1]–[3]. For example, in China Southern Power Grid,
an ±800 kV/8000 MW ‘Kun-Liu-Long’ ultra-high-voltage
MTVSC-HVDC transmission system was put into operation,
and AC/DC power grid now includes eight AC and eleven DC
transmission channels [4]. Different operation characteristics
and control modes of the HVDC transmission system will have
signiﬁcant impact on the operation state of the entire AC/DC
power system and will also affect static voltage stability
degree of the system. In addition, with many renewable energy
generation stations connected to the power grid, uncertain
ﬂuctuation of their power outputs will result in uncertain
ﬂuctuation of the system operation state, which brings great
challenges to maintain voltage stability of the AC/DC power
system [5], [6]. Static voltage stability margin (SVSM) is a
commonly used index for evaluating static voltage stability
degree of a power system, which represents maximum load
growth the system can bear in the current operation state [5]–
[7]. Therefore, it is urgent to propose an SVSM calculation
method for AC/DC power systems with LCC-HVDC and
MTVSC-HVDC considering uncertain renewable energy out-
put.
Recently, several publications have focused on SVS analysis
of AC/DC power systems. Reference [8] analyzed the inﬂu-
ence of VSC-HVDC on LCC-HVDC at the same bus, and it
also analyzed the SVS of the system, including LCC-HVDC
or VSC-HVDC, with maximum available power as the index.
In [9], a single-infeed model is derived to represent a multi-
infeed DC transmission system, and the effective short-circuit
ratio is applied to voltage stability analysis of a single-infeed
HVDC system was extended to analyze stability of a multi-
infeed HVDC system. Reference [10] proposed a general SVS
analysis method, deduced a general voltage stability index
called the hybrid generalized short circuit ratio, and solved
voltage stability critical point of the hybrid multi-infeed DC
system. Reference [11] proposed a control algorithm based on
the VSC-HVDC system to improve SVS, which showed VSC
control input will affect the local and global SVSM. Based on
the aforementioned studies, it can be concluded establishing an
accurate steady-state model of LCC-HVDC and VSC-HVDC
converter stations is helpful to reﬂect power ﬂow distribution
of the system more accurately. However, in SVS analysis of the
aforementioned studies, the control mode of HVDC was ﬁxed
and did not take into account the control mode of HVDC will
change with load growth in the system [12], [13]. Switching
of the HVDC control mode will affect calculation results of
the SVSM of an AC/DC power system, so it is necessary to
model switching of control modes in SVSM calculation.
For a power system integrating numerous RESs, if the
uncertainty of RES output is considered, SVSM of the system
will be an uncertain quantity instead of a deﬁnite value [14].
Interval method is widely used for uncertain analysis because
it only needs to give RES output range in advance without
excessive sampling, and RES output range is easy to obtain
according to historical operation data. In [15], [16], interval
number was used to describe uncertainty of RES output, and
corresponding SVSM interval was calculated by the afﬁne
interval algorithm and continuous power ﬂow method. Ref-
erence [17] proposed the interval optimization algorithm and
the OPF method to calculate the SVSM interval considering
uncertain RES output. However, aforementioned studies only
investigated calculation of SVSM interval under a ﬁxed load
growth direction (LGD), i.e., initial LGD, and did not consider
uncertainty of LGD in actual operation of the power grid.
There are two main methods for considering uncertainty of
LGD. One is to calculate SVSM corresponding to various
possible LGDs to form a boundary of the SVS region, as
shown in [18]. Another is to analyze the worst case of the
system considering uncertain LGD to assess SVS, which im-
poses less computation burden. References [19], [20] proposed
a calculation method for the local closest bifurcation point to
the current operation point. Minimum SVSM from the load
power parameter space to the local closest bifurcation point
was used as the voltage collapse index. Considering uncertain
LGD, [21] introduced the calculation method for the worst-
case SVSM. However, the aforementioned studies only applied
the proposed methods to pure AC power systems and did not
consider uncertain RES output. Therefore, how to calculate
the worst-case SVSM interval of an AC/DC power system
considering uncertain RES output and the uncertain LGD still
requires further research.
The contributions of this paper are as follows: 1) A method
to identify the worst-case SVSM interval of an AC/DC power
system with LCC-HVDC and MTVSC-HVDC transmission
lines considering control mode switching of DC converter
stations is proposed, along with the hypercone model to
describe uncertain LGD. 2) Two TLOPF models are con-
structed to solve two bounds of the worst-case SVSM interval
of an AC/DC power system, and a method to transform
TLOPF models into single-level convex optimization models
for solution is proposed. The proposed method has much
higher computational efﬁciency than the Monte Carlo or Latin
976 CSEE JOURNAL OF POWER AND ENERGY SYSTEMS, VOL. 10, NO. 3, MAY 2024
hypercube sampling method, which can be applied to the
worst-case SVSM identiﬁcation in actual large-scale AC/DC
systems accurately and efﬁciently.
The rest of this paper is organized as follows. Section II
presents worst-case SVSM identiﬁcation model for AC/DC
power systems based on the OPF method and two TLOPF
models for worst-case SVSM interval identiﬁcation. Sec-
tion III proposes the solution method for three-level optimiza-
tion models. Section IV details case studies on a modiﬁed
IEEE-39 bus system and an actual 8733 bus AC/DC power
grid in China. Section V presents the conclusions.

conclusion.text:
V. C ONCLUSION
In this study, an identiﬁcation method for worst-case SVSM
interval of AC/DC power systems considering uncertain RES
output is proposed. The proposed method uses a hypercone
model to describe LGD uncertainty. A bi-level identiﬁcation
model is established to solve worst-case SVSM. Two TLOPF
models are proposed to identify worst-case SVSM interval
with uncertain RES output. Control mode switching of DC
converter station along with load growth is considered in
calculation models. The two TLOPF models can both be
transformed into max–min bi-level OPF models at ﬁrst. By
transforming inner level model into its dual form, bi-level
max–min OPF models can be transformed into two single-level
optimization models for solution. Case studies on modiﬁed
IEEE-39 bus AC/DC system and an actual AC/DC power grid
in China indicate correctness and efﬁciency of the proposed
method. Moreover, obtained worst-case SVSM intervals are
more conservative than traditional SVSM intervals under the
initial LGD.
This study only calculates worst-case SVSM intervals of
AC/DC power systems considering uncertainties of LGD and
renewables. In actual operation of an AC/DC power grid,
worst-case SVSM value must be bigger than allowable secure
level. Thus, our future approach will be to increase worst-
case SVSM value by adjusting system operation parameters
986 CSEE JOURNAL OF POWER AND ENERGY SYSTEMS, VOL. 10, NO. 3, MAY 2024
and implementing some control measures, especially by es-
tablishing a new control mode of HVDC transmission system
with some methods.
